claims.text: The dynamic mechanical behavior of FCC CoCrFeMnNi HEAs is governed by competition between dislocation glide and deformation twinning.
Lattice distortion influences the competition between dislocation glide and deformation twinning.
Stacking-fault energy influences the competition between dislocation glide and deformation twinning.
Grain size influences the competition between dislocation glide and deformation twinning.
The initial CoCrFeMnNi HEA is face-centered cubic.
CoCrFeMnNi will exhibit greater strength than conventional alloys having similar composition and microstructure.
CoCrFeMnNi will exhibit greater ductility than conventional alloys having similar composition and microstructure.
The dominant deformation mechanism will transition from dislocation glide to deformation twinning as strain rate increases.
The dominant deformation mechanism will transition from dislocation glide to deformation twinning as temperature increases.
The proposed mechanism applies to FCC CoCrFeMnNi over strain rates from 10^-4 to 10^2 s^-1.
The proposed mechanism applies to FCC CoCrFeMnNi over temperatures from 298 K to 873 K.
The transition point between dislocation-dominated and twinning-dominated deformation depends on alloy composition.
The transition point between dislocation-dominated and twinning-dominated deformation depends on microstructure.
